units.title: Myeloid Progenitor Lineages, Thrombopoiesis (Early vs Late), Megakaryocyte Stages & Morphological Variants
units.sec: Myeloid Progenitor Lineages, Thrombopoiesis (Early vs Late), Megakaryocyte Stages & Morphological Variants
units.guide:
Lineages & thrombopoiesis (p169): common myeloid progenitor → RBC, granulocyte, monocyte, megakaryocyte → platelet; thrombopoietin boxed as 'From kidneys and liver' acting on the myeloid stem cell. Thrombopoiesis → Early requires thrombopoietin ('From liver'), IL-3 (platelet development) and IL-11 (recombinant = Oprelvekin, for chemotherapy-induced thrombocytopenia); Late requires SDF-1.
Megakaryocyte maturation: myeloid stem cell → megakaryoblast → megakaryocyte → platelet precursor extensions → platelets; Stage II basophilic, Stage III maximal granules with multilobed nuclei, Stage IV mature with lesser granules and pyknotic nuclei; endomitosis = multiplication of megakaryocytes.
Morphological variations (photos): giant megakaryocyte in ITP, dwarf in CML, cloud in primary myelofibrosis, staghorn in essential thrombocytosis.

units.title: Platelet Counts, Lifespan, Sample Handling, Pseudothrombocytopenia & Platelet Transfusion (SDP vs RDP)
units.sec: Platelet Counts, Lifespan, Sample Handling, Pseudothrombocytopenia & Platelet Transfusion (SDP vs RDP)
units.guide:
Basics (p170): lifespan 10 days, normal 1.5–4 lakh/µL, life span in stored blood 72 hrs; thresholds — thrombocytopenia < 1,00,000/µL, bleeding < 20,000/µL, significant bleeding < 10,000/µL.
Investigations: coagulation studies need platelet poor plasma, platelet studies need platelet rich plasma, all at room temperature except lupus anticoagulant at 4°C. Pseudothrombocytopenia = satellitism, caused by EDTA, clumping of platelets, remedied by re-sampling in 3.2% trisodium citrate.
Transfusion: complete within 20 mins; SDP = apheresis/costly, RDP = pooling & centrifugation/cheap/commonly used; 1 unit SDP or 4–6 units RDP raise the count by 30,000–50,000/µL, whereas 1 unit RDP alone raises it by 6,000/µL.

units.title: Platelet Cascade I: Endothelial Antiplatelet/Anticoagulant/Fibrinolytic Roles, vWF Adhesion Receptors & Granules
units.sec: Platelet Cascade I: Endothelial Antiplatelet/Anticoagulant/Fibrinolytic Roles, vWF Adhesion Receptors & Granules
units.guide:
Adhesion (p171): endothelial injury is mandatory; endothelium is antithrombotic, subendothelium prothrombotic. Antiplatelet = PGI₂, nitric oxide, ADPase. Anticoagulant = heparin-like molecules (with AT-III, inactivating II, IX, X, XI, XII), thrombomodulin (thrombin → protein C → inactivates V and VIII), TFPI (inactivates VII and X; tissue factor = III). Fibrinolysis = release of tPA.
Adhesion mechanism: endothelial injury → release of vWF; sources megakaryocyte and endothelium (coiled form in Weibel-Palade granule); receptors Gp VI on collagen and Gp Ib-IX on platelet.
Activation/degranulation: α granules and δ (dense) granules, the latter carrying ADP > ATP, calcium, histamine, serotonin. Aggregation: Gp IIb-IIIa with fibrinogen binding to platelets.

units.sec: Clotting Cascade (Intrinsic, Extrinsic, Common), Fibrinolysis Checkpoints, Antifibrinolytics & aPTT/PT Tests
units.guide:
Clotting cascade (p172): intrinsic (in vitro) with back amplification of thrombin — XII → XIIa (high molecular weight kininogen, kallikrein), XI → XIa, IX → IXa (vIII, Ca²⁺, phospholipid), then X → Xa (vII, Ca²⁺); extrinsic (in vivo) — endothelial injury → thromboplastin/tissue factor (factor III) with calcium and phospholipid → factor VIIa, converging on factor X.
Common cascade: X → Xa → prothrombin → thrombin (factor II) with calcium phospholipase va → fibrinogen → fibrin → clot stabilisation by XIII. Fibrinolysis: tPA converts plasminogen to plasmin, generating FDPs; check points are protein C and S (V, VIII), t-PA and TFPI; t-PA inhibitors that promote thrombosis are α-2 antiplasmin, TAFI, PAI and lipoprotein A.
Tests: aPTT assesses intrinsic and common cascade with poor sensitivity; PT assesses extrinsic and common cascade.
